problem: De novo IDP-targeted antibody design has not broken the interface-confidence ceiling (A-beta42 ipTM ~0.12-0.14 vs >0.3 aspirational binder target). The existing production path designs and scores against a single extracted ordered window and uses contact counting, not confidence.

hypotheses.h1_ensemble_robust_ranking: Ensemble-robust interface PAE (25th percentile across K conformations) ranks candidates more stably than single-conformation scoring, because it rejects candidates that score well in only one conformation.
hypotheses.h2_disorder_guided_design: Injecting the per-residue disorder profile into BFN sampling (epitope_disorder_profile / disorder_guided, currently exploratory and unwired in production) plus ensemble scoring raises achievable interface confidence relative to disorder-agnostic design.

protocol.design: CDR redesign via run_bfn_design (Complex mode), disorder-guided ON vs OFF (H2 factor)
protocol.validation: AF2 multimer interface PAE against all 5 conformations (single-sequence, 3 recycle)
protocol.scoring: robust interface PAE = 25th percentile across 5 conformations (lower is better)
protocol.confidence_policy: PAE only; ipTM and pLDDT are abstained per publication/candidate_interface_pae_deployment_v1.json

success_gates.g1_robust_pair_accuracy: robust-PAE ranking separates designed vs composition-shuffle controls with pair accuracy >= 0.65 and cluster-bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0.5
success_gates.g2_ensemble_improvement: ensemble-robust (p25) ranking is more stable than single-conformation ranking, measured by higher control-vs-design separation or lower bootstrap dispersion

claim_boundary: This is an exploratory R&D experiment. Success of H1/H2 does not establish a validated IDP binder; it only establishes whether ensemble-aware design and robust scoring improve the interface-confidence signal. Wet-lab validation remains required for any binding claim.
